key_idea: Sort by start ascending and, on ties, by end descending; then every interval containing the current one has already been processed, and it only needs max convincingness among processed intervals with end >= its end.
sketch: Compress end points (a+t) and keep a Fenwick tree for prefix maximum over reversed end coordinates (i.e. suffix max over ends), initialised to -1. Process in sorted order: ans = 1 + query(end >= my end), then update at my end. O(n log n). Pitfalls: tie-breaking on equal starts (longer first) and equal ends with earlier start (naturally handled by start order); ends reach 2e9 so use 64-bit; output in input order. Stress-tested against a memoised brute force.
